### Observed differences

- In the later window, A20's outgoing transitions changed from going to A27/A28 (about 45/55) to going almost always to A21 (98%). [DIR001]
- A23's outgoing transitions changed from always to A24 to going to A27/A28 (about 50/50). [DIR002]
- A27 and A28 no longer go to A21; instead they go to A24 (and A28 also to A27). [DIR003, DIR004]
- A21 and A23 now occur earlier in the trace (mean position dropped by about 0.07), while A27 and A28 occur later (mean position rose by about 0.10). [POS001-POS004]
- The relative order flipped: A21 and A23 now precede A27 and A28 in about 98% of cases, whereas before they followed them. [REL001-REL004]
- Lags confirm: A20 to A21 changed from lag 3 to lag 1; A20 to A27/A28 changed from lag 1/2 to lag 4/5; A27/A28 to A24 changed from lag 4/5 to lag 1/2. [LAG001-LAG008]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a hypothesis that the order of activities changed: A27 and A28, which previously occurred early (right after A20) and before A21/A23, now occur later (after A21/A23) and before A24. A21 and A23 moved earlier. This is directly shown by the successor changes (DIR), position shifts (POS), relative order flips (REL), and lag changes (LAG), all consistent with each other. The number of qualifying items (20) is far above the 0.39 expected by chance. A competing explanation of sampling variation in variant frequencies is unlikely given the magnitude and consistency of the changes across all indicators. A limitation is that the evidence does not show whether this reflects a deliberate process redesign or a different execution pattern, but the structural change in ordering is well supported.
